_comment: Where NPC schedules are read from, and how their headings are read.
THE FINDING THAT SHAPES THIS FILE: the wiki has schedules for two of the
thirty-four villagers. Adeline and Celine have full four-season, seven-day
tables. Every other `<Name>/Schedule` subpage exists and is empty — a tab
header and nothing under it. Checked across the whole roster, 2026-08-07.
The plan called for 'the 12 romanceables first'. That is not available from
this source at any effort, so the parser is built for the whole cast and the
coverage report carries the remaining thirty-two as gaps. When a page gets
filled in, `pnpm enrich:pages` picks it up with no code change.
SEASON HEADINGS are `== {{Season|Spring}} Schedules ==`. The template is
reduced to its last argument before matching, so what a rule sees is the word
'Spring'.
WHAT IS NOT INGESTED, and why. Two heading groups select between several
tables using state the player cannot see:
- Rainy schedules are chosen by a hidden rainy-day counter, with a separate
winter variant. The wiki says so itself.
- Friday Night at the Inn schedules are chosen by how many FNATI events
have already happened, and there are three kinds.
Both are extracted into `sources/` so the data is not lost, and neither
becomes a schedule entry. First-match-wins would pick variant #1 and present
a coin flip as a fact. The schedule records a `rain_variants` or
`friday_variants` gap instead, which is the true answer: it varies, and here
is how many ways.
QUEST-GATED DAYS *are* ingested. 'Before / After Repair the Bridge is
complete' is exactly what priority-ordered overrides are for: the 'after'
entry sits above the 'before' one and carries the quest requirement, so a
save that has finished the quest matches it and every other save falls
through. No negation operator needed.
_variant_comment: Heading text that marks a group of tables selected by hidden state. Matched
case-insensitively as a prefix of the section heading.
_gate_comment: A `==== … ====` heading that gates a day on a story quest. `after` marks the
table that applies once the quest is done, and it is given the higher
priority; `before` is the fallthrough and carries no requirement.
